1.2 Session protocol

The TIP (Transaction Information Protocol) feed uses SoupBinTCP as its session protocol. SoupBinTCP provides a mechanism for authentication and recovery of messages. All TIP messages are sent as sequenced data packets. Please see the SoupBinTCP specification for details.

1.3 Session flow

The client connects to the server and issues a Login request packet with username, password and sequence number. If the login request is successful, the server responds with a Login accepted packet followed by Sequenced data packets containing TIP messages. The stream of sequenced data packets ends when the system is closed. The last packet on the session is an end of session packet.

Please note that specifying 0 (zero) in the sequence number field will give the same result as 1 (one). This is a deviation from the SoupBinTCP specification, which states that 0 (zero) will start the message sequence from the most recently generated message.

If the login request is unsuccessful, the server reponds with a Login rejected packet with a reason code. The server closes the connection after sending the Login rejected packet.

1.4 TIP Message Format

The TIP protocol is a tagged text protocol.

A TIP message is a sequence of tag and value pairs separated with semicolon.

A tag is zero or more UPPERCASE characters followed by a lowercase character. The tag is followed immediately by the value. Examples of tags are "FLd", "STa".

The first tag in a message is always the message type. The message type tag has no value. An example of a message type tag is "BDSh".

TIP message are encoded with UTF-8 unless stated otherwise.

The maximum length of a TIP message is indicated with the constant MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH (4096 bytes).

Any max field length excludes any escape characters '\'.

No empty values will be sent; exceptions are message type tags and Boolean tags (the presence of the tag itself corresponds to a 'true' value).

For a decimal field (i.e. the Float data type) the length is given as X,Y where X is the max number of digits in the integer part of the field (left of the separator). Y is the number of decimals (rigth of the separator).

The order of the disseminated tags is not fixed, i.e. the client may not make any assumptions of the order of tags. The only fixed component of a message is the message type, which is always placed first in the message data.

Note that new messages and fields may be added in future versions of the protocol. To ensure forward compatibility, clients should ignore unrecognized message types and field tags.

1.5 Special characters and escape characters

Some characters have a special meaning when they appear in values:

  • Field delimiter ';' (semicolon)
  • Index delimiter ':' (colon)
  • Value delimiter ',' (comma)
  • \ = Escape character '\' (backslash)

When special characters are part of the value itself, they are prefixed with the escape character '\'. The client should treat the next character as a regular character, not as a special character.

An example: "NAmSmith\, Jones\, Wesson\, Inc.;" should be parsed to yield a value string of "Smith, Jones, Wesson, Inc.".

Note that escape characters can cause a field to exceed its maximum length. TIP clients need to be able to handle this situation.

1.6 Key fields

A key field is a field which will always be present in a message. Key fields often serve as idetiifers for entities referenced in the message.

The following key types are available:

  • TK (GENIUM™ Market Info key)

    Fields with this key type contain a GENIUM™ Market Info generated id that uniquely identifies a reference data entity. The most common member of this key type is the Id field. The Id key is unique within the reference data namespace.

    GENIUM™ Market Info will ensure that the id is stable over time (i.e. a specifc share will not change its id value from one day to another). Customers should always build their internal basic data structures based on the id value.

  • IK (Information key) Fields with this key type contain the source system's internal identifiers.

1.7 Data model

Basic data messages provide static, or reference, data such as Exchange, Market, Tradable. Each entity is uniquely identified by an Id. Exchange, market, list, index and sector are "container" entities, i.e. they have zero or more child entities. The child entities will reference their parent entity by the Id of the parent. Thus, it is possible in a client program to build a hierarchy of entities.

Real-time messages provide data such as Trade, Orderbook, List update, Index update and more. Each real-time message reference the basic data entity the information pertains to by the unique entity Id.

The client can also expect a number of messages from the server that are not part of the data feed itself. These messages provide information about the state of the feed. EndOfStream is sent when the system closes. EndOfBasicData indicates that the basic data for a source system is complete. Please see each section below for details.

2. Basic Field Types

Each TIP field has an associated field type or enumeration determining the value range.

Name
Length
Description
Boolean
A boolean flag; the presence of the tag indicates a 'true' value and if the tag is missing indicates a 'false' value.
Char
1
Single character, E.g.'A', '-'.
Date
8
A date value with format YYYYMMDD. E.g. '20040324'.
Double
High precision signed or unsigned floating point number. E.g '0.00000001', '1234.21332123'
Float
Signed or unsigned floating point number. E.g. '0.25', '-1', '34'.
Floatlist
One or more floats separated by the list item separation character. E.g. '123.13,-2.67'.
Id
10
A GENIUM™ Market Info feed assigned information entity id. Fields with this field type is numeric number. Can never be a negative value (unsigned).
Idlist
One or more information entity ids separated by the list item separation character. E.g. '101,102'.
Ifloat
Indexed float. A value pair consisting of an index integer and a float value separated by the index separation character. E.g. '1:23.25', '7:0.25'.
Iinteger
Indexed integer. A value pair consisting of an index integer and an integer value separated by the index separation character.
Integer
20
Single unsigned or signed number, e.g. 123, -2. The default length is 19 for the integer and 1 for the sign.
Integerlist
One or more integers separated by the list item separation character. E.g. '123,-2'.
Istringlist
Indexed stringlist. A value pair consisting of an index integer and a stringlist field separated by the index separation character. E.g. "7:AVA,SHB,SEB". The length given at the field level is per string entity and not for the whole field since the list is dynamic (i.e. the string length would be 3 for AVA in the example above).
Iyesno
Indexed boolean. A value pair consisting of an index integer and a Yes or No flag separated by the index separation character. E.g. '1:Y', '2:N'.
String
Character string, e.g. "Ericsson B", "001234AB".
Stringlist
One or more strings separated by the list item separation character. E.g. "AVA,SHB,SEB". The length given at the field level is per string entity and not for the whole field since the list is dynamic (i.e. the string length would be 3 for AVA in the example above).
Time
10
A time value with format HHMMSS[.mmm] (24-hour clock), e.g. '222324.102' or '090031'. The '.mmm' (millisecond) portion is optional. In general, timestamps on real-time messages refer to the timezone of the sending source system.
YesNo
1
Yes or No flag. Indicates for example if the trade should update last paid or not. 'Y' indicates a Yes/Positive/True value and 'N' a No/Negative/False value.

4. Messages

4.1 Reply messages

EndOfBasicData

This message indicates that the initial basic data load from the source system has been completed. Please note that multiple messages may be sent for the same source system. Also note that there may be hot updated or hot inserted basic data entities in the real-time feed after the end of basic data message.

Example:

EOBd;s1;

Message type: EOBd

4.5 Basic Data - Miscellaneous

BasicDataTableEntry

This is a generic table entry message. It covers complementary static information such as stop codes (codes at trading halt), notification codes, trade types etc.

The purpose of the BasicDataTableEntry message type is to provide identifiers for stop codes, notification codes and trade types guaranteed to be unique for all sources. This is necessary since each source has it own set of trade types etc, whose identifiers might overlap with those used by other sources. In the real-time messages, identifiers for trade types etc refer to a BasicDataTableEntry entity, which in turn points out the source specific information. Hence, information receivers should use the BasicDataTableEntry messages, which will be sent as part of the basic data information, as a mapping table to identify the source specific trade type etc.

Note 1. The BasicDataTableEntry message is not used for broker information. The TableEntryType field contains a value for brokers, but this is not used.

Orderbook3

The Orderbook message contains price level updates for a tradable security. The message is the most frequent message in the TIP feed and is designed to be compact while at the same time being easy to parse and process.

The Orderbook message only contains information that has changed; the client must maintain the state of the order book and update the changed price levels from the message. An order book message may contain more than one level.

(Bid/Ask)PriceAtLevel could be "0 (zero)". Or it may not exist at level, then it is required from vendors to set the price field to null.

In this example of an Orderbook message the first bid level has changed, while other levels remain unchanged.

p;i375;s2;t154413.882;h1:1;b1:60.00;g1:400;

In this example, ask levels 1-3 have changed and ask level 4 has been deleted.

p;i54;s2;t172313.144;a1:34.5;j1:4000;k1:6;a2:35;j2:7000;k2:10;a3:35.5;j3:3000;k3:4;e4;

A special type of Orderbook message is sent when all price levels of the tradable security are cancelled, for example when the market of the tradable security has closed.

p;i54;s2;t173000.675;Of;

OrderbookSummary

This message is used to transmit a summary of price and volume information for a business day. The message can be transmitted more than once every day. The message is normally transmitted twice a day, before and after trading, however markets may trade during the evening and then cause additional orderbook summary messages to be triggered when certain states changes occur. The market data system can be configured to send out summary messages dependent on the market, and which summary message that is the official "closing prices". Hence customers are urged not to hardcode any behaviour regarding when (at which state) official closing prices are triggered. The market data system tries to fill in as much information as possible.

Note the following:

1. Values calculated during the night might have been added or corrected in comparison to the message sent, after trading, on the previous trading day. The official orderbook summary message is most likely to be disseminated when the market closes in the evening.

2. The Date field contains information on the day that the values refer to. Normally the previous trading day if it is the opening closing price and the current date if it is the closing price of the current day's trading.

3. OrderbookSummary messages can be transmitted as both basic and real-time data.

4. High and Low prices in OrderbookSummary messages are not adjusted according to corporate actions and price type changes.

TurnoverListUpdate

This message holds the turnover and tendency of Turnover lists (number of increased/decreased best bids/paid prices). The turnover and tendency are calculated by the market data system at regular intervals.

Note that if there is no data available for the previous trading day for tradable securities that are members of a list, they will be counted as UnchangedBids and UnchangedPaid. This is most likely to occur on the first trading day of a tradable security.
